thread:
Ben (ML): Ran a focused sweep comparing streaming vs non-streaming endpoints with the new int8-quant kernel + small-kernel-fuse on A100/us-west1 and H100/europe-west1. Uploading the short notes and a couple of p99/p50 plots. TL;DR: streaming improves p50 a lot but has a tail tradeoff under high fanout unless we enable fastpath caching.
Anya: nice! which workload + seq len?
Ben (ML): eval workload = prod-like chat trace (avg seq 220 tokens, median 120). Concurrency sweep 50->2000 requests/s. Batch window 6 for non-stream; streaming uses SSE with 50ms coalescing. Kernel: int8-quant + fused-attn-small.
Sam H: can you paste the key numbers? p50/p99 and throughput (tok/s)?
Ben (ML): paste below — numbers are steady-state single-region. A100/us-west1: non-stream p50=120ms p99=420ms throughput=36k tok/s; streaming p50=65ms p99=610ms throughput=42k tok/s. H100/europe-west1: non-stream p50=95ms p99=360ms throughput=48k tok/s; streaming p50=50ms p99=540ms throughput=56k tok/s.
Lee: interesting that streaming boosts tok/s by ~15% but p99 jumps ~30-40%. Did you try enabling prefix/KV cache?
Ben (ML): yes — enabling KV prefix reduces p99 for streaming by ~120-150ms on H100, ~90-110ms on A100. With KV cache + fastpath: streaming p99 drops to 380ms (A100) and 320ms (H100). So combined config gives streaming both higher throughput and maintained tail latency.
Maria: what about polyglot/quant quality regressions? any change after int8?
Ben (ML): small quality delta measured on held-out eval set: avg logprob delta ~ -0.02, BLEU-style proxy -0.6 pts. Worth flagging but within acceptable threshold for experiments. We'll run longer eval for hallucination checks.
Sam H: were kernels identical across regions? or any microcode differences?
Ben (ML): kernel build was identical (same docker hash), but driver versions diff: us-west1 A100 drivers are 525.x, europe H100s had 551.x — kernel perf differs slightly, explains part of raw tok/s delta. Will reproduce cross-region with matched drivers.
Anya: can you attach the small ASCII SLO chart? helps for PM/infra readout.
Ben (ML): pasted quick ascii summary: 
```
Throughput (tok/s)      p50 (ms)    p99 (ms)
A100 non-stream   36k         120         420
A100 streaming    42k          65         610
A100 streaming+KV 40k          70         380
H100 non-stream   48k          95         360
H100 streaming    56k          50         540
H100 streaming+KV 53k          55         320
```
Sam H: good. for rollout suggestion: default to non-stream for heavy-fanout low-p99 customers, and streaming+KV+fastpath for latency-sensitive p50 customers. Add a routing policy?
Lee: agree. Also add autoscale headroom limits to streaming endpoints to prevent sudden fanout from spiking KV misses.
Maria: I'll create an entry in the eval-runbook noting the quant quality delta and link to the longer eval.
Ben (ML): thanks. Next actions: (1) reproduce H100 vs A100 with matched drivers (Ben), (2) baseline long-run hallucination/quality checks (Maria), (3) propose routing policy + config flags for streaming on console (Anya + Lee).
deploy-bot: scheduled job "ml/throughput-sweep-171999" created, runs in 12h and will post artifacts in #eng-ml.
Sam H: perfect. can we also include one permissive canary with quant-int8 for selected tenants so we can monitor customer-observed regressions?
Ben (ML): yes — I'll set up a small canary group (5 tenants) next week. Will post the canary config and metrics link here. :rocket:
Anya: thanks — this helps clarify the tradeoffs for product.
Lee: assigning follow-up tickets in sprint board for infra limits + routing policy.
Ben (ML): uploaded graphs and raw csv to the artifacts link in the job. will ping when processed.
